source.title: Taming Curvature: Architecture Warm-Up for Stable Transformer Training
source.authors: Sameera Ramasinghe; Thalaiyasingam Ajanthan; H. M. Dolatabadi; C. H. Koneputugodage; Gil Avraham; Violetta Shevchenko; Yan Zuo; Karolina Pająk; Alexander Long

record.file_problem: Whole paper text, including supplementary material, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own curvature and training-stability results on Transformers, refining the depth-related claim under tested settings; it does not measure CIFAR classification error or the other claim versions directly.
record.gate_note: The paper tests depth-related training stability and reports curvature, loss spikes, divergence, and convergence outcomes. It does not report training classification error on CIFAR, random labels, local minima, initialization comparisons, or the other version-specific outcomes. Curvature measures are relevant to V3's depth/stability argument, but do not themselves establish training classification error.
record.test_reason: The study uses edge-of-stability theory to design and evaluate Transformer stabilization. Its depth experiments measure language-model loss and curvature in residual Transformers, not V3's plain convolutional networks versus identity-shortcut networks. It does not test V5's recovery above an initial linearized stability limit, full-batch threshold hovering with falling loss, or divergence from a documented below-threshold start.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors propose efficient warm-started curvature estimation and architecture warm-up, reporting a wider stable learning-rate range, fewer loss spikes, and improved Transformer training reliability. Their empirical depth association is not a proof that curvature must increase with depth.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains large decoder-only Transformers on language corpora and manipulates effective depth to control optimizer stability; the claim versions primarily concern classification error, local minima, initialization, shortcuts, learning-rate stability, and batch normalization.
record.method_sensitivity: Depth (8, 16, and 32 layers) changes curvature and stability; peak learning rate changes baseline stability; architecture warm-up changes stability; tested unlock spacing is reported as not highly sensitive.

fits_no_version.finding: At peak learning rate 0.008 on FineWeb, the 8-layer/640M residual Transformer converges stably, while the 16-layer/1B and 32-layer/3B models exhibit curvature spikes and divergence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing Transformer depth and size together can increase curvature and destabilize training under a fixed learning-rate recipe.

fits_no_version.finding: Architecture warm-up broadens the tested stable learning-rate range and can replace learning-rate warmup with comparable convergence; tested unlock spacings give similar results.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Temporarily restricting effective Transformer depth and later unlocking zero-initialized blocks can stabilize language-model training.

fits_no_version.finding: Sections 9.1–9.2 report curvature settling into a lower band and adaptive preconditioning partially damping curvature spikes. The plotted quantities are normalized and do not establish threshold hovering with continuing loss reduction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive preconditioning can partially stabilize Transformer curvature, but this feedback can fail during rapid spikes.

record.problems: The depth comparison is on FineWeb Transformers and reports loss and curvature, not training classification error. The plotted comparisons do not provide per-condition numeric values in the supplied text. The paper itself notes that its curvature upper bound does not prove curvature must strictly increase with depth.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying reported outcomes were omitted. The paper's additional stabilization-method comparisons and validation perplexities do not measure the training-error outcomes named in these claim versions.

untested.parts: All parts: near-zero CIFAR training classification error, including random or corrupted labels, and model-size or training-recipe qualifications.
All parts: teacher-student ReLU spurious minima and extra student neurons.
All parts: depth degradation in plain batch-normalized convolutional networks, prevention by identity shortcuts, and the tanh-initialization and Fixup qualifications.

All parts: activation-matched initialization and signal propagation, orthogonal-versus-Gaussian training speed, and trainable depth. Zero-initialized block unlocking is not a comparison testing these claims.

Recovery above the initial linearized stability limit in wide squared-loss networks; full-batch sharpness hovering at the threshold while loss falls; and divergence despite a documented below-threshold start. The adaptive Transformer curvature observations do not establish these conditions.
All parts: batch-normalization speed and learning-rate tolerance comparisons, and Fixup training without normalization.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are assessed against the supplied claim versions; cannot_determine does not dispute the reported Transformer outcomes. No qualifying version-specific results are missing. The supplied paper does not establish the record's ICLR peer-review designation.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification error; corrupted or random labels; size, initialization, duration, early stopping, and regularization effects.
Teacher-student ReLU local minima and the effect of student width relative to teacher width.
No CIFAR-10 or ImageNet training classification error comparison; no plain versus identity-shortcut experiment; tested depth and stability on decoder-only Transformers with residual blocks.
Activation-matched, orthogonal, Gaussian, or convolution-kernel initialization comparisons and resulting trainable depth.
Learning rates above the initial stability limit, loss recovery/divergence from such rates, and sharpness hovering at the threshold.
Batch-normalization comparisons and Fixup-style training without normalization.

rows.subject: 8-layer (640M) model
rows.operation_detail: Train decoder-only Transformer on FineWeb with peak learning rate 8 × 10−3; track training loss and curvature.
rows.measure: Training loss trajectory and raw/preconditioned curvature
rows.value: Maintains lower curvature and converges stably; curvature measures are normalized.
rows.note: The text contrasts this depth with the 16- and 32-layer models; it does not state a classification-error measure.
rows.check: The stable 8-layer residual Transformer measures a different architecture and outcome from V3. Its normalized curvature and loss trajectory do not establish any V5 trajectory relative to the specified stability limits.

rows.subject: 16-layer (1B) model
rows.operation_detail: Train decoder-only Transformer on FineWeb with peak learning rate 8 × 10−3; track training loss and curvature.
rows.measure: Training loss trajectory and raw/preconditioned curvature
rows.value: Pronounced curvature spikes during learning-rate warmup, crossing the stability boundary and diverging.
rows.note: This is a Transformer depth/stability result, not a reported classification-error result.
rows.check: The reported divergence is correctly attributed to the 16-layer Transformer, but it is not a reversal of V3: no plain-versus-shortcut convolutional comparison is made. Initial position relative to the stability threshold is not reported.

rows.subject: 32-layer (3B) model
rows.operation_detail: Train decoder-only Transformer on FineWeb with peak learning rate 8 × 10−3; track training loss and curvature.
rows.measure: Training loss trajectory and raw/preconditioned curvature
rows.value: Pronounced curvature spikes during learning-rate warmup, crossing the stability boundary and diverging.
rows.note: This is a Transformer depth/stability result, not a reported classification-error result.
rows.check: The reported divergence is correctly attributed to the 32-layer Transformer, but it is not a reversal of V3. Depth and parameter count increase together, and neither V3's architectural comparison nor V5's specified starting-threshold conditions are tested.

rows.subject: 16-layer (1B) models with architecture warm-up
rows.operation_detail: Train with architecture warm-up and compare peak-learning-rate sweeps with an unaltered baseline.

conditions.value: half depth through learning-rate warmup, then unlock remaining layers

rows.measure: Training loss stability and preconditioned curvature
rows.baseline: Vanilla networks without architecture warm-up under the same settings exhibit rapid curvature escalation and unstable convergence.
rows.value: Maintains bounded preconditioned curvature and avoids loss spikes; stable convergence across the tested learning-rate range.
rows.note: The text reports the comparison in aggregate and does not give separate numeric loss values for each rate.
rows.check: This is performance of the study's stabilization method, outside the claim versions. Section 4.4 and Figure 4 do not explicitly identify the model as 16 layers/1B; that attribution should be qualified.

rows.subject: 16-layer (1B) vanilla baseline
rows.operation_detail: Train without architecture warm-up under the same peak-learning-rate sweep settings.
rows.measure: Training loss stability and preconditioned curvature
rows.value: Increasingly unstable as peak learning rate increases; rapid curvature escalation and unstable convergence.
rows.note: The text reports the comparison in aggregate and does not give separate numeric loss values for each rate.
rows.check: This is a comparator for the study's stabilization method, not reversed evidence for V3. Here vanilla means no architecture warm-up; the Transformer still has residual connections. Section 4.4 does not explicitly establish the stated model size.

rows.subject: 16-layer (1B) Transformer with architecture warm-up only
rows.operation_detail: Remove learning-rate warmup from the baseline configuration and enable architecture warm-up.
rows.baseline: Baseline with standard learning-rate warmup; on-par convergence is reported.
rows.value: Attains on-par convergence while exhibiting more stable training than the learning-rate-warmup baseline.
rows.note: No numeric training classification error is reported.
rows.check: Replacing learning-rate warmup with architecture warm-up measures the study's method performance, not any supplied version. The reported convergence comparison is faithful; its configuration also specifies weight decay 0.1.

rows.subject: 16-layer (1B) model with architecture warm-up
rows.operation_detail: Train with architecture warm-up and compare architecture warm-up unlock schedules.
rows.value: Results are described as similar; method is described as not highly sensitive to schedule spacing.
rows.note: The paper states the schedules have similar results without supplying numerical values.
rows.check: This schedule-sensitivity ablation concerns the study's own method and should not be a claim-evidence row. Section 11 does not explicitly state the model size attached to this row.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
